notes: Review is scoped to the 12-Pokémon Beta 2 slice.
The six original beta Pokémon remain the starter team; the other six enter through Roster Ranch.
Regular Roster M-A provides a captured pull count of 10; Vanguard economy costs remain explicit local-beta configuration.
Beta v3 adds reviewed Sunny Day, Rain Dance, Chlorophyll, Rain Dish, Heat Rock and Damp Rock as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks 5/8-turn weather, 1.5/0.5 damage, doubled weather Speed and Rain Dish 1/16 recovery.
Beta v4 adds reviewed Tailwind, Reflect, Light Screen and Light Clay as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Tailwind duration/Speed, screen duration/damage modifiers, critical bypass and Light Clay extension.
Beta v5 adds reviewed Grassy Terrain, Misty Terrain and Terrain Extender as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks five-turn terrain, Terrain Extender eight-turn duration, Grassy grounded healing/Grass boost/quake-like reduction, and Misty grounded status/confusion protection plus Dragon damage reduction.

Grounding support for this slice covers Flying types and the already-modelled Magnet Rise/Telekinesis volatile flags; Levitate, Air Balloon, Gravity and other grounding overrides remain blocked for future mechanics batches.
Beta v6 adds reviewed Spikes for Chesnaught and Stealth Rock for Infernape as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Spikes at 1/8, 1/6 and 1/4 max HP for grounded switch-ins, plus Stealth Rock at Rock effectiveness × 1/8 max HP.
Hazards share the R3-20 entry/replacement lifecycle. Heavy-Duty Boots, hazard removal, Magic Guard and additional grounding overrides remain fail-closed until their own reviewed batches.
Showdown sim/battle.ts cross-checks tied SwitchIn side-condition handlers resolving by stable creation effectOrder.
Beta v7 adds reviewed Rapid Spin for Blastoise and Defog for Decidueye/Scizor as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Rapid Spin cleanup only after a successful damaging hit, removal of Leech Seed and user-side entry hazards, plus a +1 Speed secondary boost.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Defog lowering target Evasion, removing Reflect/Light Screen from the target side, clearing supported entry hazards from both sides, and clearing active terrain.
Beta v8 adds reviewed Toxic Spikes for Beedrill as an optional Training choice; default builds remain unchanged.

Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Toxic Spikes at two layers: grounded entrants receive poison at one layer or bad poison at two layers; grounded Poison types absorb the condition, while Steel and ungrounded targets are unaffected.

Rapid Spin and Defog cleanup now include Toxic Spikes in the pinned Showdown hazard-removal order. Heavy-Duty Boots, Magic Guard, Sticky Web, Court Change and additional grounding overrides remain fail-closed.
Beta v9 promotes reviewed Wonder Room for Primarina as an optional Training choice; default builds remain unchanged.
Showdown commit aa17ca0f cross-checks Room duration at five turns and same-Room recast toggling the pseudo-weather off rather than refreshing it.
Wonder Room swaps Defense and Sp. Def base stats before applying the stage modifier for the requested defensive stat.
Trick Room and Magic Room core mechanics are implemented and regression-tested but remain unavailable in Beta v9 because none of the 12 reviewed species has a legal M-A relation to those moves.

Trick Room uses priority -7 and dynamic reversed Speed ordering within an action priority bracket; Magic Room suppresses held-item passive effects while leaving Ability effects and Mega evolution eligibility outside that suppression contract.
Beta v10 promotes reviewed Yawn for Blastoise and Perish Song for Primarina as optional Training choices; default builds remain unchanged.

Pinned Showdown/Champions evidence cross-checks Yawn as a two-residual delayed sleep: protection and grounded Electric Terrain block scheduling, while sleep immunity/status rules are rechecked when the delayed effect resolves.

Perish Song assigns an initial perish count of 4 to each currently active eligible Pokémon, decrements at the end of every turn including the use turn, faints at count 0 without damage, and switching clears the counter.

The shared delayed-effect scheduler resolves after existing end-turn HP residual groups and before ordinary field/condition expiry, preserves deterministic RNG, and stores delayed state on the affected Pokémon so ordinary switching removes it.
Soundproof/Baton Pass transfer semantics, Future Sight-style delayed attacks, two-turn moves and recharge turns remain fail-closed until dedicated reviewed batches.
